title: Bootstrapping Wilson lines in Critical Bosonic QED$_3$ Part 1: Large-$N$ endpoint correlators and CFT data
authors: Jun Maeda, Toshiki Onagi, Soichiro Shimamori
abstract: We study the conformal Wilson line with general charge $q$ in critical bosonic QED$_3$ with $N$ complex scalar flavors by combining diagrammatic four-point calculations with endpoint crossing. We formulate the endpoint crossing equations with the full $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ flavor structure, keeping positivity manifest. For arbitrary positive integer charge $q$ held fixed at large $N$, we obtain closed-form expressions for four-endpoint correlators and mixed correlators involving two bulk Hubbard--Stratonovich fields through first subleading order in $1/N$. These results determine the endpoint dimension, the defect $g$-function, and the dimensions and endpoint OPE coefficients of the lowest non-singlet Wilson-line primaries. Moreover, combining the diagrammatic correlator with endpoint crossing, somewhat surprisingly, we find agreement between the bulk and Wilson-line spectra in every non-singlet flavor channel through order $1/N$. At degenerate levels, this agreement concerns the OPE-weighted averages of anomalous dimensions probed by the endpoint correlator. For unit charge, we independently reproduce these averages from the known bulk higher-spin spectrum.
summary: This paper applies the conformal bootstrap program to study charged Wilson lines in critical bosonic QED$_3$. By combining diagrammatic calculations with endpoint crossing, the authors derive key conformal data, such as dimensions and OPE coefficients, for these lines. The results confirm consistency between bulk and defect spectra, providing a detailed understanding of the theory's critical behavior in the large-N limit.
main_problem: To systematically determine the conformal data (dimensions and OPE coefficients) of charged Wilson lines and their endpoints in a critical gauge theory.
main_result: The authors obtained closed-form expressions for four-endpoint correlators and demonstrated agreement between the bulk and Wilson-line spectra up to the first subleading order in 1/N.
method: The study combines diagrammatic four-point calculations with the application of endpoint crossing equations, utilizing the large-N expansion.
model_or_system: The physical system is critical bosonic QED$_3$ with $N$ complex scalar flavors, which is equivalent to the critical $	ext{CP}^{N-1}$ model. The analysis focuses on Wilson lines $W_q(C)$ and associated endpoint operators.
key_observables: Endpoint dimension, defect $g$-function, dimensions, and endpoint OPE coefficients of non-singlet Wilson-line primaries.
important_parameters: Large-$N$ limit with fixed charge $q$ ($q=O(N^0)$); calculations are performed up to first subleading order in $1/N$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the validity of the endpoint bootstrap program and is restricted to the first subleading order in $1/N$.
figures_summary: Not specified in the provided notes.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by introducing the framework of Wilson lines and endpoint operators, calculating four-endpoint correlators using crossing relations, and finally addressing mixed correlators involving the bulk Hubbard-Stratonovich field.
why_interesting: While focused on gauge theory, the use of conformal bootstrap techniques and the study of critical points are fundamental tools applicable to strongly correlated electron systems, particularly those exhibiting quantum criticality.

figures.caption: Figure 2. A defect-changing operator inserted on a straight Wilson line. With τ increasing from left to right, ϕab A (τ0) changes the defect from Da to Db. The double lines denote the two Wilson defects and the black dot denotes the local insertion.

Figure 3. Schematic OPE of two compatible defect-changing operators. The adjacent sectors Da →Db →Dc combine into a single defect-changing insertion from Da to Dc. The OPE coefficients and the powers of τ in (2.20) are suppressed.

Figure 5. The complete order-1/N diagram classes, illustrated for q = 2 in the sector m = 1. The four black dots are ordered as (1, 2, 3, 4), and one scalar propagator joins each of (12), (34), (14), and (32). A dashed line is the effective σ propagator, a wavy line is the effective photon, and a double line is a physical charge-two Wilson segment. In each panel the interaction is attached to every admissible scalar propagator or Wilson segment. Seagull tadpoles and the critical-mass insertion are scaleless in dimensional regularization; line-tension and endpoint counterterms cancel in the normalized correlator.

Figure 7. The two nonlocal diagram classes contributing to the mixed correlator at order 1/N, shown for q = 2 with τ1 < τ2 < τ3 < τ4 from left to right. The endpoint pair is joined by the charge-two Wilson segment and by two scalar propagators. In panel (a), both external σ fields attach to the same scalar propagator while the other scalar propagator has no σ insertion. In panel (b), they attach to different scalar propagators. Solid curves denote scalar propagators, dashed curves denote external σ propagators, and the double line denotes the Wilson segment. For general charge q, the respective multiplicities are q and q(q −1).

Figure 8. The integration region responsible for the logarithmic divergence of I12|14 σ . The dashed σ propagator joins an interaction vertex w on the scalar propagator (12) to a vertex w′ on (14). On the right, both vertices approach x1, while all external endpoints remain fixed. Double lines denote the physical Wilson segments C12 and C34; the other scalar propagators are omitted. The curves indicate propagator connectivity, not particle trajectories.
